title: We included half a million people in the financial system by granting them their first loan
summary: Lima, May 13, 2025. Credicorp, a leading financial holding company in Peru with a presence in Colombia, Chile, Bolivia, Panama, and Miami, presented its
body_text: In 2024, 541,000 people received their first loan through Yape, thereby entering the formal financial system. Between 2020 and 2024, Credicorp financially included 5.7 million people throughout Peru by Yape and BCP. Lima, May 13, 2025. Credicorp, a leading financial holding company in Peru with a presence in Colombia, Chile, Bolivia, Panama, and Miami, presented its sustainability report. The group reported that 541,000 people were included in the formal financial system through loans granted by Yape. Between 2020 and 2024, the group included 5.7 million people in the formal financial system. The main drivers of financial inclusion were Yape and BCP, by means of enrollment and use of the mobile app and the opening of savings accounts, respectively. Fifty percent of those financially included during this period were women. “Through Credicorp’s Financial Inclusion Index, we monitor progress in this area. For example, we identified that 28% of the Peruvian adult population is at the advanced level of financial inclusion, almost double the figure in 2021, when only 15% were at that level. This means that almost a third of Peruvians use financial tools efficiently and frequently. However, there is still a long way to go,” said Darice Gubbins, Credicorp’s Sustainability Leader. For its part, Mibanco banked more than 58,000 people in 2024, 62% of whom were women. Furthermore, advancing its efforts to democratize access to insurance, Pacífico issued more than 3.6 million inclusive insurance policies last year. These policies, so named because they offer more affordable premiums of between S/1 and S/30, have protected more than 2.4 million people. Commitment to financial education During 2024, BCP’s behavioral change programs helped more than 345,000 clients improve their financial behavior by overcoming debt, regularizing their late payments, and overcoming credit card overdrafts. In addition, Yape provided training to more than 165,000 people in personal finance and small business management. “ Our financial education programs seek to encourage individuals, businesses, and society in general to adopt increasingly healthy financial behaviors that contribute to their long-term financial well-being . In this way, we generate a positive and lasting impact, ” highlighted Darice Gubbins, Credicorp’s Sustainability Leader. Meanwhile, Pacifico Seguros´ Comunidad Segura program reached 88,000 people and strengthened its risk prevention culture, with 93% of participants identifying safe areas in their homes in case of an emergency. Additionally, via Credicorp Capital’s Invirtiendo Futuros program, corporate volunteers provided specialized financial mentoring to high-impact companies. Boosting sustainable finance In 2024, Credicorp disbursed more than US$1.5 billion in sustainable loans through BCP, promoting environmentally and socially responsible business practices. The bank also awarded its first Sustainability Award. A US$100 million Sustainability Linked Loan (LLO ) was provided to a mining company to finance the development of its operations in the country. Its indicators include efficient water management and other social issues. The group expanded its carbon footprint measurement to include its priority portfolios, such as BCP’s wholesale banking and the investment portfolios of Prima AFP and Pacífico Seguros. It also published its second Task Force report. Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) . In it, it presented progress on various climate management fronts, including the results of its own carbon footprint measurement, which showed a 23% reduction in net emissions compared to the 2022 base year, in line with its commitment to achieving carbon neutrality in its operations by 2032. Continuous integration into strategy The holding company continually seeks to integrate and align its sustainability strategy with its corporate strategy. Thus, in 2024, after creating the position of Chief Strategy Officer (CSO),the Sustainability Office became his responsibility, demonstrating the high level of integration with the group’s strategy. “Our sustainability strategy is supported by strong corporate governance, which integrates this vision into senior management decision-making. In fact, in the executive segment’s compensation model, we have specific indicators linked to sustainability,” commented Darice Gubbins, Credicorp’s Sustainability Leader. The sustainability report is available here .

title: SEO-Roadmap: So erstellen Sie eine + Kostenlose Vorlage
summary: Ein SEO-Roadmap-Dokument beschreibt die Schritte zur Verbesserung der Suchmaschinenperformance Ihrer Website. Lerne, wie man einen erstellt.
body_text: Wir haben diesen Artikel aus dem Englischen ins Deutsche übertragen. Klicke hier , um den Originalartikel zu lesen. Wenn dir am Inhalt Probleme auffallen, schicke uns gerne eine Nachricht an report-osteam@semrush.com . Was ist eine SEO-Roadmap? Ein SEO-Fahrplan ist ein Dokument, das einen schrittweisen Plan zur Verbesserung der Suchmaschinenleistung Ihrer Website formalisiert. Komplett mit Aufgaben, Zeitplänen und Verantwortlichen. Es ist auf Ihre individuellen SEO-Ziele zugeschnitten. Und das Arbeiten an diesen Zielen sollte Ihnen letztendlich helfen, Ihre übergeordneten Geschäftsziele zu erreichen. Sie können eine SEO-Roadmap mithilfe eines Google Sheets oder eines anderen Projektmanagement-Tools erstellen. Hier ein Beispiel, wie das aussehen könnte: Laden Sie unsere kostenlose SEO-Roadmap-Vorlage herunter um dem Rest dieser Anleitung folgen zu können. Warum Sie einen SEO-Plan benötigen Hier sind einige Möglichkeiten, wie Ihnen eine SEO-Roadmap hilft: Komplexe Aufgaben vereinfachen Ein SEO-Fahrplan unterteilt den SEO-Prozess in kleinere, besser handhabbare Aufgaben. Anstatt beispielsweise allgemein das Ziel „SEO verbessern“ anzustreben, könnte der Fahrplan mit einer spezifischen Keyword-Recherche beginnen. Und dann geht es an die Optimierung einzelner Seiten. Maßnahmen mit hoher Wirkung priorisieren Die Verwendung eines Fahrplans hilft Ihnen, sich auf Maßnahmen zu konzentrieren, die den größten Nutzen bringen. Damit Sie keine Zeit mit Dingen verschwenden, die keine Auswirkungen haben. Wenn beispielsweise der größte Teil Ihres organischen Traffics von einigen wenigen, besonders erfolgreichen Seiten stammt, könnte Ihre Roadmap die Optimierung dieser Inhalte priorisieren, bevor Sie neue Seiten erstellen. Anpassung an Suchmaschinen-Updates Ihr Fahrplan ist ein lebendiges Dokument. So können Sie es als Reaktion auf Änderungen des Suchmaschinenalgorithmus anpassen. Um sicherzustellen, dass Ihre SEO-Maßnahmen langfristig wirksam bleiben. Wenn Google beispielsweise in Zukunft den Fokus stärker auf Kennzahlen zur Nutzererfahrung (UX) legt, könnte sich Ihre Roadmap ändern und die Verbesserung der Navigation mit benutzerfreundlichen Menüs über alles andere stellen. Wie man eine SEO-Roadmap erstellt und verwendet Die Erstellung und Umsetzung einer SEO-Roadmap erfordert viel Vorplanung und Zusammenarbeit. So geht's: 1. Definieren Sie Ihre SEO-Ziele Klare SEO-Ziele helfen Ihnen, sich auf die wirkungsvollsten Taktiken zu konzentrieren (die wir in Schritt acht genauer behandeln werden). Und bietet Ihnen eine klare Möglichkeit, den Erfolg später zu messen. Beginnen Sie damit, festzulegen, was Sie mit Ihren SEO-Maßnahmen erreichen möchten. Ob es nun um die Steigerung der Markenbekanntheit, die Generierung von Leads oder etwas anderes geht. Setzen Sie sich anschließend spezifische, messbare, erreichbare, relevante und terminierte (SMART) Ziele, um sicherzustellen, dass Ihre Ziele klar und umsetzbar sind. Nehmen wir an, Ihr Unternehmen möchte den Online-Umsatz im nächsten Jahr um 10 % steigern. Sie unterstützen dies, indem Sie sich ein SEO-Ziel setzen, den organischen Traffic innerhalb der nächsten neun Monate um 25 % zu steigern. Was Sie angesichts Ihres Budgets und Ihrer Ressourcen für erreichbar halten. Ihr wichtigster Leistungsindikator (KPI) ist der organische Traffic. Aber vielleicht möchten Sie noch ein paar weitere SEO KPIs festlegen, wie z. B. Keyword-Rankings und Klickrate (CTR). Legen Sie anschließend klare Zeitpläne fest, um sicherzustellen, dass Ihr Team auf Kurs bleibt und kontinuierlich Fortschritte in Richtung Ihrer Ziele erzielt. Beachten Sie bei der Festlegung der Zeitpläne für Ihre Aufgaben folgende Tipps: Berücksichtigen Sie die Arbeitsbelastung und sonstige Verpflichtungen der Teammitglieder, um bei Ihren Zeitschätzungen realistisch zu sein. Gestalten Sie Ihre Zeitpläne flexibler, um unerwartete Herausforderungen oder Verzögerungen bewältigen zu können. Überprüfen und passen Sie Ihre Zeitpläne regelmäßig an, je nach Fortschritt, Prioritätenänderungen oder neuen Informationen. 2. Analysieren Sie Ihre SEO-KPIs. Die Analyse Ihrer aktuellen Leistung anhand der von Ihnen festgelegten KPIs kann Ihnen helfen zu verstehen, wie stark Sie sich verbessern müssen, um Ihr Ziel zu erreichen. Nehmen wir an, Ihre KPIs sind Keyword-Rankings und organischer Traffic. Sie sollten für jede dieser Kennzahlen Ausgangswerte ermitteln. Und vielleicht noch einige ergänzende Informationen. Verwenden Sie Google Analytics, um den organischen Traffic zu verfolgen. Melden Sie sich bei Ihrem GA-Konto an und gehen Sie zum Tab " Berichte ". Klicken Sie anschließend auf „ Akquisition ” > “ Traffic-Akquise .“ Sie sehen den gesamten Datenverkehr für den ausgewählten Zeitraum aufgeschlüsselt nach Kanal. Achten Sie besonders auf die Zeile „Organische Suche“ – denn hier wird angegeben, wie viel organischen Traffic Ihre Website erhält. Öffnen Sie das Tool und erstellen Sie ein Projekt, falls Sie dies noch nicht getan haben. Geben Sie als Nächstes Ihre Domain ein und klicken Sie auf " Tracking einrichten ." Schließen Sie die Konfiguration ab. (Folgen Sie dieser Einrichtungsanleitung , falls Sie Hilfe benötigen.) Sobald die Einrichtung abgeschlossen ist, wird Ihnen ein „Landschafts“-Bericht angezeigt. Diese Übersicht fasst die Sichtbarkeit Ihrer Domain, den geschätzten Traffic und die durchschnittliche Position für Ihre verfolgten Keywords zusammen. Gehen Sie zum Tab „ Übersicht “ und scrollen Sie nach unten zum Abschnitt „Ranglistenübersicht“. Dieser Abschnitt zeigt, wo Ihre Website für einzelne Schlüsselwörter rangiert und wie sich diese Positionen im Vergleich zum letzten Zeitraum verändert haben. Das Verständnis Ihrer aktuellen Keyword-Rankings und Ihres organischen Traffics hilft Ihnen, Ihre Fortschritte zu messen. 3. Führen Sie ein technisches Audit durch Und Dinge, die sich auf die Benutzererfahrung (UX) auswirken – Benutzererfahrung im SEO bezieht sich darauf, wie einfach Besucher auf Ihrer Website navigieren und mit ihr interagieren können. Eine gute UX ist besonders wichtig, weil sie die Absprungrate senken und Besucher dazu anregen kann, weitere Seiten zu erkunden. Und die Bereitstellung einer positiven UX kann Ihre SEO-Performance steigern. Finden Sie diese Probleme mit dem Tool „Site Audit“ von Semrush . Öffnen Sie das Tool, geben Sie Ihre Domain ein und klicken Sie auf " Start Audit ." Sie sehen die „Einstellungen für die Website-Überprüfung“. Schließen Sie die Konfiguration ab, um Ihren ersten Website-Crawl einzurichten, und klicken Sie auf „ Website-Audit starten .“ (Folgen Sie dieser Einrichtungsanleitung , falls Sie Hilfe benötigen.) Sobald das Audit abgeschlossen ist, wird Ihnen ein „Übersichtsbericht“ angezeigt. Als Erstes sollten Sie sich den Site Health Score ansehen. Die Berechnung basiert auf der Anzahl der auf Ihrer Website gefundenen Fehler und Warnungen. Je höher diese Zahl, desto besser. Gehen Sie anschließend auf die Registerkarte " Probleme ", um die Liste der Probleme auf Ihrer Website anzuzeigen. Sie sehen dann die „Fehler“, die die schwerwiegendsten sind. Neben „Warnungen“ auch Probleme mittlerer Schwere. Und „Hinweise“ – nicht kritische Punkte, die es zu beachten gilt. Klicken Sie bei einzelnen Problemen auf " Warum und wie man es behebt ", um mehr über das Problem und seine Lösung zu erfahren. Notieren Sie sich die hier aufgeführten Punkte, damit Sie priorisieren können, welche Sie in Ihre Roadmap aufnehmen möchten. 4. Entdecken Sie Optimierungsmöglichkeiten auf der Seite. On-Page-SEO hilft Suchmaschinen, den Inhalt Ihrer Seiten zu verstehen, und erhöht so die Chancen auf ein höheres Ranking in den Suchergebnissen für relevante Keywords. Zu den wichtigsten Elementen einer Seite gehören Seitentitel (auch H1s genannt), Überschriften, Meta-Beschreibungen (HTML-Code, der eine Seite kurz zusammenfasst) und die URL-Struktur. Nutzen Sie den On-Page-SEO-Checker von Semrush , um Ideen zur Verbesserung der On-Page-SEO Ihrer Website zu erhalten. Öffnen Sie das Tool, geben Sie Ihre Domain ein und klicken Sie auf " Ideen erhalten ." Schließen Sie die Konfiguration ab. (Folgen Sie dieser Einrichtungsanleitung , falls Sie Hilfe benötigen.) Sobald das Tool bereit ist, wird Ihnen ein „Übersichtsbericht“ wie dieser angezeigt: Wechseln Sie zum Tab „ Optimierungsideen “. Sie finden seitenbezogene Ideen zu Strategie, Inhalten, Backlinks, Semantik, Benutzererfahrung usw. Klicken Sie neben einer der Seiten auf „ # Ideen “, um die Empfehlungen zur Verbesserung der Onpage-SEO anzuzeigen. Anschließend können Sie die Ideen in den Kategorien „Strategie“ und „Inhalt“ gruppiert sehen. Im Inhaltsbereich erfahren Sie beispielsweise, ob Sie Ihre Ziel-Keywords in die H1-Überschrift, den Hauptteil der Seite und andere wichtige Bereiche einbauen müssen. Überprüfen Sie die Ideen. Die wichtigsten Punkte fügst du später deiner Roadmap hinzu. Die Idee ist, jede Seite für Ihre Zielgruppe relevant und wertvoll zu gestalten. Daher ist es wahrscheinlicher, dass es von Suchmaschinen in den Suchergebnissen erscheint. Weiterführende Informationen : Checkliste für On-Page-SEO: Die vollständige Aufgabenliste für 2024 5. Überprüfen Sie Ihr Backlink-Profil Relevante Backlinks (Links auf anderen Seiten, die auf Ihre Seite verweisen) von autoritativen Websites können Ihr Suchmaschinenranking verbessern. Es ist also eine gute Idee zu wissen, wo man aktuell steht. Analysiere dein aktuelles Backlink-Profil mit Backlinks . Das Tool zeigt Ihnen die Anzahl der Backlinks an, die auf Ihre Website verweisen. Und weitere Einblicke. Öffnen Sie das Tool, geben Sie Ihre Domain ein und klicken Sie auf „ Analysieren .“ Im Bericht „Übersicht“ sehen Sie Ihren „Autoritätswert“, der den allgemeinen Zustand Ihrer Website auf einer Skala von 100 misst. Und Ihr „Gesamttoxizitätswert“ – eine Einschätzung, wie viele minderwertige Backlinks auf Ihre Website verweisen. Es ist ratsam, beide Kennzahlen gemeinsam zu betrachten. Wenn Ihr Authority Score niedrig und Ihr Toxizitätswert hoch ist, deutet dies darauf hin, dass Sie daran arbeiten sollten, mehr Links von relevanten, qualitativ hochwertigen Websites zu erhalten. Wechseln Sie anschließend zum Tab " Backlinks ", um eine detaillierte Ansicht der einzelnen Backlinks zu erhalten. Und entfernen oder verleugnen Sie sie. Mit diesem Tool können Sie auch das Backlink-Profil Ihrer Website mit dem Ihrer Konkurrenten vergleichen. Fügen Sie die Domains Ihrer Konkurrenten hinzu, und Sie erhalten einen Vergleichsbericht. Wenn Sie feststellen, dass Ihre Konkurrenten mehr hochwertige Backlinks von branchenrelevanten Websites besitzen, könnten Sie erwägen, diese Websites zu kontaktieren, um Backlinks zu erhalten. Notieren Sie sich die jeweils nächsten Schritte, damit Sie beim Erstellen Ihrer SEO-Roadmap festlegen können, wie Sie vorgehen sollen. Weiterführende Informationen : So führen Sie ein Backlink-Audit durch (5 einfache Schritte) 6. Neue Content-Möglichkeiten identifizieren Die Erkenntnis, welche Inhalte am besten ankommen, gibt Aufschluss darüber, was Ihre Besucher schätzen. So können Sie diesen Erfolg in Zukunft wiederholen. Gehen Sie zu „ Berichte ” > " Engagement " > " Seiten und Bildschirme .“ Scrollen Sie nach unten, um die Liste der Seiten mit Aufrufen, Nutzern, durchschnittlicher Verweildauer und anderen Datenpunkten zu sehen. Analysieren Sie diese Daten, um zu verstehen, welche Themen bei Ihrer Zielgruppe Anklang finden. Wenn Sie beispielsweise feststellen, dass Ihre ausführlichen Leitfäden regelmäßig mehr Besucher und Interaktionen anziehen als kürzere Blogbeiträge, können Sie sich künftig auf die Erstellung umfassenderer Inhalte konzentrieren. Finden Sie außerdem Content-Lücken – Themen, die sich um Schlüsselwörter drehen, für die Ihre Konkurrenten gute Platzierungen erzielen, Sie aber nicht. Öffnen Sie das Tool, geben Sie Ihre Domain und die Domains Ihrer Konkurrenten ein und klicken Sie auf " Vergleichen ." Sie sehen eine Liste gängiger Schlüsselwörter, für die alle Websites ein gutes Ranking erzielen. Klicken Sie auf „ Fehlend “, um die Keywords anzuzeigen, für die alle Ihre Konkurrenten ein Ranking erzielen, Sie aber nicht. Klicken Sie anschließend auf „ Schwach “, um Keywords anzuzeigen, für die Ihre Website ein niedrigeres Ranking als Ihre Konkurrenten aufweist. Durch das Aufdecken dieser Keyword-Lücken können Sie Inhalte zu Themen erstellen, die bisher unerschlossene Zielgruppenbedürfnisse erfüllen. Notieren Sie sich nun alle Keywords, auf die Sie abzielen möchten, und alle Inhalte, die Sie erstellen möchten. So können Sie sie in Ihre SEO-Strategie einbeziehen. Weiterführende Informationen : So finden Sie & Keywords der Konkurrenz analysieren 7. Liste alle deine SEO-Aufgaben auf Stellen Sie nun eine umfassende Liste von SEO-Aufgaben zusammen, basierend auf den Erkenntnissen aus Ihrem technischen Audit, Onpage-SEO-Audit, Backlink-Analyse und Keyword-Recherche . Nehmen wir an, Ihre Liste sieht folgendermaßen aus: Optimieren Sie Seitentitel, Meta-Beschreibungen und Überschriften-Tags. Verbesserung der Mobilfreundlichkeit Defekte Links und Crawling-Fehler beheben Adressierung doppelter Inhalte Vereinfachen Sie die Architektur Ihrer Website. Verbessern Sie Ihre interne Verlinkungsstruktur. Bilder optimieren Verbessern Sie die Überschriftenstruktur innerhalb des Inhalts Schema-Markup implementieren Schlüsselwörter auswerten Schlüsselwortliste finalisieren Inhaltskalender des Plans Erstellen Sie neue Inhalte, die auf hochwertige Schlüsselwörter abzielen. Aktualisieren Sie bestehende Inhalte, um deren Relevanz und Qualität zu verbessern. Hochwertige Backlinks von autoritativen Websites erstellen Verfolge nicht verlinkte Erwähnungen, um sie in Backlinks umzuwandeln. Als nächstes gruppieren Sie diese Aufgaben in Hauptfokusbereiche – Keyword-Recherche, On-Page-Optimierung, technische SEO, Content-Erstellung und Linkaufbau . 8. Prioritäre Handlungsfelder identifizieren Die Priorisierung Ihrer SEO-Aufgaben hilft Ihnen, einen fokussierten Aktionsplan zu erstellen, der Ihre Ergebnisse maximiert und Ihr Team auf die wichtigsten Ziele ausrichtet. Das bedeutet, dass nicht jede Aufgabe es in Ihren endgültigen Zeitplan schaffen wird. Wie können Sie Ihre Aufgaben priorisieren? Hier sind einige Faktoren, die Sie berücksichtigen sollten: Ausrichtung auf Ihre SEO-Ziele Mögliche Auswirkungen Für die Umsetzung erforderlicher Aufwand Abhängigkeit von anderen Aufgaben oder Ressourcen Ein effektiver Ansatz ist die Verwendung einer Prioritätsmatrix, in der Sie jede Aufgabe anhand ihrer Auswirkungen und ihres Aufwands eintragen. Aufgaben, die in den Quadranten „Schnelle Erfolge“ fallen (hohe Wirkung und geringer Aufwand), sollten zuerst angegangen werden. Weil sie den größten Nutzen bei geringstem Investitionsaufwand bieten. Elemente im Quadranten „Große Risiken“ (hohe Auswirkungen, hoher Aufwand) sollten sorgfältig geplant und ausgeführt werden. „Füllpunkte“ (mit geringem Aufwand und geringem Einfluss) können verwendet werden, um Lücken in Ihrem SEO-Roadmap-Dokument zu füllen, sofern Sie dafür Platz haben. „Undankbare Aufgaben“ (geringe Wirkung, hoher Aufwand) sollten entweder weggelassen oder zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt neu bewertet werden. Beispielsweise könnte die Aktualisierung der Titel-Tags für wichtige Seiten ein „schneller Erfolg“ sein, während eine überarbeitete Website-Architektur eine „große Investition“ darstellen könnte. 9. Meilensteine zur Fortschrittsverfolgung festlegen Meilensteine sind wichtige Kontrollpunkte auf Ihrem Weg zur Suchmaschinenoptimierung, die den Fortschritt in Richtung Ihrer Ziele verdeutlichen. Sie bieten Ihnen einen Überblick über Ihren Gesamtfortschritt. Ihre Meilensteine könnten beispielsweise Folgendes umfassen: Abschluss der technischen SEO-Verbesserungen bis zum Ende des ersten Quartals Veröffentlichung von 10 neuen, auf Schlüsselwörter ausgerichteten Blogbeiträgen bis zum Ende des zweiten Quartals Aktualisierung aller Top-Inhalte bis zum Ende des dritten Quartals Und denken Sie daran, regelmäßig Ihren Fortschritt zu überprüfen. Wir empfehlen, dies jeden Monat zu tun und in der entsprechenden Spalte Ihrer Tabelle eine Notiz zu machen. 10. Ressourcen zuweisen Eine effektive Ressourcenallokation stellt sicher, dass Sie über die notwendigen Fähigkeiten und Werkzeuge verfügen, um Ihren Plan umzusetzen. Beginnen Sie damit, den Ressourcenbedarf für jede Aufgabe Ihrer Prioritätenliste zu ermitteln. Dies kann Folgendes umfassen: Zeitaufwand für interne Mitarbeiter (z. B. Content-Ersteller, Entwickler und SEO-Spezialisten) Externe Expertise (z. B. Freiberufler, Agenturen und Berater) Tools (z. B. SEO-Tools, Analysetools und ein Content-Management-System) Auf Grundlage dieser Einschätzung sollten Sie Ihre verfügbaren Ressourcen zunächst den Aufgaben mit der höchsten Priorität zuweisen. Seien Sie realistisch, was Sie mit Ihren aktuellen Ressourcen erreichen können, und überlegen Sie, ob zusätzliche Investitionen notwendig sind, um Ihre Ziele zu erreichen (und innerhalb Ihres Budgets zu bleiben). Abschließend sollten bestimmte Teammitglieder oder externe Partner mit der Ausführung und Berichterstattung über die einzelnen Punkte beauftragt werden. Und notieren Sie es in Ihrer Tabelle. Dadurch wird sichergestellt, dass jeder seine Rolle kennt und zum Gesamterfolg Ihrer SEO-Strategie beiträgt. 11. Zusammenarbeit mit Interessengruppen Die Kommunikation mit den Stakeholdern ist entscheidend, um deren Zustimmung für Ihre SEO-Strategie zu erhalten. Und später seinen Erfolg unter Beweis zu stellen. Beginnen Sie damit, Ihren Fahrplan den wichtigsten Interessengruppen vorzustellen. Sammeln Sie ihr Feedback und klären Sie etwaige Bedenken. Am wichtigsten ist, dass Sie bereit sind, Ihren Fahrplan bei Bedarf anzupassen. Geschäftliche Prioritäten können sich ändern, und der Input von Interessengruppen kann wertvolle Perspektiven einbringen. Sobald Sie mit der Umsetzung des Fahrplans begonnen haben, sollten Sie die Stakeholder regelmäßig über den Fortschritt Ihrer SEO-Maßnahmen informieren. Und teilen Sie uns mit, wie Ihre Fortschritte hinsichtlich Ihrer KPIs aussehen. 12. Ergebnisse auswerten und Roadmap überarbeiten SEO ist ein fortlaufender Prozess, kein einmaliges Projekt. Ihre SEO-Roadmap sollte also ein lebendiges Dokument sein, das sich mit Ihren Fortschritten und Erkenntnissen weiterentwickelt. Ein typischer SEO-Plan hat eine Laufzeit von sechs bis zwölf Monaten. Sobald Sie alle Aufgaben des ursprünglichen Fahrplans abgeschlossen haben, ist es an der Zeit, Ihre KPIs auszuwerten, um zu sehen, ob Sie Ihre Ziele erreicht haben. Falls ja, erstellen Sie einen neuen Fahrplan, der auf Ihren bisherigen Fortschritten aufbaut und Punkte berücksichtigt, die Sie im ersten Fahrplan nicht angehen konnten. Wenn sich Ihre erste Roadmap beispielsweise stark auf Keyword-Recherche und technische Optimierungen konzentrierte, könnte Ihre nächste Roadmap die Erstellung von Inhalten rund um diese Keywords und den Aufbau hochwertiger Backlinks priorisieren. Wenn Sie Ihre Ziele nicht erreicht haben, müssen Sie möglicherweise einen Fahrplan erstellen, der neue Herausforderungen angeht. Oder Sie müssen Ihre Ziele möglicherweise anpassen. Weiterführende Informationen : SEO-Ergebnisse: So verfolgen Sie die SEO-Performance & SEO-Performance messen Schaffen Sie eine solide Grundlage mit einer SEO-Roadmap Eine effektive SEO-Roadmap nutzt Daten, um genaue Schritte und Aufgaben zu definieren. Nutzen Sie die richtigen Werkzeuge, um diese Daten zu erhalten. Beginnen Sie mit einer Überprüfung Ihrer Website, um ein besseres Verständnis ihrer SEO-Stärken und -Schwächen zu erlangen. Melden Sie sich kostenlos bei Semrush an, um mit Site Audit zu beginnen.

title: Nouvelle réforme des IJSS : ce qui change au 1er avril 2025 !
summary: Le premier trimestre 2025 apporte son lot d’évolutions réglementaires concernant les IJSS
body_text: Le décret n° 2025-160 du 20 février 2025 apporte une modification importante au calcul des indemnités journalières de la Sécurité sociale (IJSS) en cas de maladie non professionnelle. À partir du 1er avril 2025 , le plafond de revenu pris en compte pour ce calcul passe de 1,8 SMIC à 1,4 SMIC . Cette évolution concerne à la fois les employeurs et les salariés des régimes général (CPAM) et agricole (MSA). Source : https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000051223695 Comment sont calculées les IJSS ? Les indemnités journalières sont destinées à compenser une partie de la perte de salaire en cas d'arrêt de travail. Leur montant est basé sur le salaire journalier de base (SJB) , qui se calcule ainsi : Salaire journalier de base = Somme des salaires bruts des 3 derniers mois / 91,25 ( 91,25 correspond à la moyenne des jours par trimestre ) Jusqu’au 31 mars 2025 , les salaires pris en compte pour ce calcul étaient plafonnés à 1,8 SMIC . Mais à compter du 1er avril 2025 , ce plafond est abaissé à 1,4 SMIC . Cela signifie que pour certains salariés, le montant des IJSS va diminuer. L’indemnité journalière correspond à 50 % du salaire journalier de base, dans la limite du nouveau plafond. Quels salariés sont concernés ? Cette réforme, applicable au 1er avril 2025 , impacte principalement les salariés dont la rémunération est supérieure à 1,4 SMIC (soit > 2 522,52€ en 2025). ➡️ Si le salaire du salarié est inférieur à 1,4 SMIC , cette réforme ne change rien pour lui. ➡️ Si le salaire du salarié est supérieur à 1,4 SMIC , ses indemnités journalières seront recalculées sur une base plus basse qu’auparavant, entraînant une diminution du montant perçu. Quelles conséquences pour les employeurs ? Les employeurs qui assurent un maintien de salaire devront potentiellement compenser une perte plus importante pour leurs salariés concernés. Exemples chiffrés : avant/après la réforme Prenons un exemple pour mieux visualiser l’effet de la réforme : 📌 En résumé : Cette réforme abaisse le plafond des revenus pris en compte pour le calcul des IJSS, ce qui entraîne une réduction des indemnités pour certains salariés. Cela se traduit par une augmentation du montant du complément de salaire à la charge des employeurs qui pratiquent le maintien de salaire.

title: Introducing Module Catalog & Insights: Reusable building blocks for your software factory
summary: Dagger Cloud customers can now discover, reuse, and track Dagger modules across their org. Less YAML, less reinvention, more shipping.
body_text: We’re kind of obsessed with reusable building blocks. Our founding team built Docker to help engineers compose complex software out of smaller, reusable parts. But the workflows used to build, test, and deploy them remained manual, complicated, and hard to reuse. So our obsession led us to create Dagger — bringing modularity and reusability to software delivery and development workflows, and turning artisanal processes into modern software factories built from reusable components. In Dagger, those reusable building blocks are called “modules.” You define modules with code and combine them to compose any kind of software delivery workflow, from simple builds to end-to-end tests to AI agents that do code reviews . But the real magic happens when teams can share and reuse one another’s modules, and when platform engineers can standardize and get visibility into the use of those building blocks. Today we’re launching Module Catalog & Insights for Dagger Cloud customers, making it easy for teams to find, reuse, and manage modules privately inside their organization. This lets you fully leverage reusable building blocks to build a modern software factory, and ship great software faster and safer. How it works: Discover, reuse, and track modules Just connect your GitHub repos through the Dagger Cloud GitHub app, and your modules automatically pop up in the new Modules tab. Everything is neatly organized in a searchable catalog. Your team won’t waste time reinventing something that already exists — if there’s a module out there for what they need, now they can find it. Each module gets autogenerated API docs in multiple languages, clear metadata, and an activity feed summarizing recent updates. This helps everyone quickly understand what each module does, trust it, and start using it right away. Traces are directly linked to modules, making it easier to track down issues and see actual usage. See what modules are popular, spot any weird patterns, and find opportunities to improve commonly used components. You also get a clear view of dependencies and dependents, so your team can spot and manage supply-chain risks early. Example: From one-off workflow to reusable building block Imagine your engineering team needs to build and ship Golang applications. The platform team creates a standardized, reusable GoApp module that uses a compliant Go version and allows installing additional packages following the company’s best practices: // Base sets up a pre-configured Golang container ready // to build and test Go applications func ( m * GoApp ) Base ( source * dagger . Directory , // project source code ) * GoApp { // return standard Go container ctr := dag. Container (). // start with a minimal approved Golang container image From ( "golang:1.24.3-alpine" ). // copy source code directory into the container WithDirectory ( "/app" , source). // set working directory inside the container WithWorkdir ( "/app" ). // add base pinned required packages WithExec ([] string { "apk" , "add" , "git==2.47.2-r0" }) return & GoApp {Container: ctr} } // WithPackage lets you install additional packages that // must be pinned to a version. func ( m * GoApp ) WithPackage ( ctx context . Context , pkg string , // project source code ) * GoApp { // return GoApp type for chaining if _, _, ok := strings. Cut (pkg, "==" ); ! ok { panic ( "cannot install packages without pinned versions" ) } m.Container = m.Container. WithExec ([] string { "apk" , "add" , pkg}) // install custom package return m } Once it’s pushed to GitHub, the module automatically shows up in your organization’s catalog. An engineer working on a new application can discover the module, check the auto-generated docs, and use it to build their application in a few lines: // Use platform team's base app module as a base Go image with a custom package // Build fetches the app code from a branch and builds the code func ( m * SomeTeamApplication ) Build ( ctx context . Context ) ( string , error ) { sourceCode := dag. Git (myRepo). Branch ( "new-feature" ). Tree () return dag. GoApp (). Base (sourceCode). WithPackage ( "zlib-dev" ). // platform team owns WithPackage in their module Build () } As more teams start shipping Golang applications they will discover and use GoApp . The platform team sees the module’s usage increasing, invests time to further improve and standardize it, and then uses Module Insights to quickly notify dependent teams about updates. This ensures everyone stays consistent and reliable across the organization. This is just one basic example. Dagger lets you build modules out of foundational building blocks like containers, directories, custom objects, and even LLMs . You can build anything from simple dev environments to complex, end-to-end workflows powered by AI agents, like automated code reviews and test setups! Get started today Module Catalog & Insights are available now in Dagger Cloud for customers on the Team plan. If you’re on the free plan or don’t have an account, you can try Module Catalog & Insights free for 14 days. Sign in to Dagger Cloud and click the new Modules tab. Read the docs for Modules and Module Catalog & Insights . Join the Discord to ask questions, give feedback, learn from your peers, or talk reusability to us. Explore the Daggerverse to browse nearly 1,500 public modules contributed by the community.

title: Zed v0.30.2 Release
summary: Zed CLI provides seamless interaction with SpiceDB clusters, allowing you to manage schemas, relationships, and permissions checks. Our v0.30.2 release adds composable schema support, automatic retries, backup functionality, and upcoming Windows package integration via Chocolatey.
body_text: Zed is the command line interface (CLI) tool that you can use to interact with your SpiceDB cluster. With it you can easily switch between clusters, write and read schemas, write and read relationships, and check for permissions. It can be launched as a standalone binary or as a Docker container. Detailed installation options documented here . Improvements in v0.30.2 Over the last few months we’ve been making many improvements to it, such as: Adding support for compilation and validation of composable schemas Adding automatic retries Adding a new zed backup command Publishing the package to Chocolatey for all Windows users (currently in review) And many other small fixes that are too many to list here. We are happy to announce that last week we released zed v0.30.2 , which includes all of these changes. In the near future we expect to be adding support for a new test syntax in schema files, which will allow you to validate that your schema and relationships work as you expect them to. Stay tuned! As you can see, we are continuously making improvements to zed. If you see anything not working as expected, or if you have an idea for a new feature, please don’t hesitate to open an issue in https://github.com/authzed/zed . Also, while you’re at it, please give us a star!

title: MicroAlgo Inc. Develops Classifier Auto-Optimization Technology Based on Variational Quantum Algorithms, Accelerating the Advancement of Quantum Machine Learning
summary: /PRNewswire/ -- MicroAlgo Inc. (the "Company" or "MicroAlgo") (NASDAQ: MLGO) announced today the launch of their latest classifier auto-optimization technology...
body_text: SHENZHEN, China , May 2, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- MicroAlgo Inc. (the "Company" or "MicroAlgo") (NASDAQ: MLGO ) announced today the launch of their latest classifier auto-optimization technology based on Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQA). This technology significantly reduces the complexity of parameter updates during training through deep optimization of the core circuit, markedly improving computational efficiency. Compared to other quantum classifiers, this optimized model has lower complexity and incorporates advanced regularization techniques, effectively preventing model overfitting and enhancing the classifier's generalization capability. The introduction of this technology marks a significant step forward in the practical application of quantum machine learning. Traditional quantum classifiers can theoretically leverage the advantages of quantum computing to accelerate machine learning tasks, but they still face numerous challenges in practical applications. Firstly, current mainstream quantum classifiers often require deep quantum circuits to achieve efficient feature mapping, which results in high optimization complexity for quantum parameters during training. Additionally, as the volume of training data increases, the computational load for parameter updates grows rapidly, leading to prolonged training times and impacting the model's practicality. MicroAlgo's classifier auto-optimization technology significantly reduces computational complexity through deep optimization of the core circuit. This approach improves upon two key aspects: circuit design and optimization algorithms. In terms of circuit design, the technology adopts a streamlined quantum circuit structure, reducing the number of quantum gates and thereby lowering the consumption of computational resources. On the optimization algorithm front, this classifier auto-optimization model employs an innovative parameter update strategy, making parameter adjustments more efficient and substantially accelerating training speed. In the training process of classifiers based on variational quantum algorithms (VQA), parameter optimization is one of the most critical steps. Generally, VQA classifiers rely on Parameterized Quantum Circuits (PQC), where updating each parameter requires computing gradients to adjust the circuit structure and minimize the loss function. However, the deeper the quantum circuit, the more complex the parameter space becomes, requiring optimization algorithms to perform more iterations to achieve convergence. Furthermore, uncertainties and noise in quantum measurements can also affect the training process, making it difficult for the model to optimize stably. Traditional optimization methods often employ strategies such as Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) or Variational Quantum Natural Gradient (VQNG) to find optimal parameters. However, these methods still face challenges such as high computational complexity, slow convergence rates, and a tendency to get trapped in local optima. Therefore, reducing the computational burden of parameter updates and improving training stability have become key factors in enhancing the performance of VQA classifiers. MicroAlgo's classifier auto-optimization technology, based on variational quantum algorithms, significantly reduces the computational complexity of parameter updates through deep optimization of the core circuit. It also incorporates innovative regularization techniques to enhance the stability and generalization capability of the training process. The core breakthroughs of this technology include the following aspects: Depth Optimization of Quantum Circuits to Reduce Computational Complexity: In traditional VQA classifier designs, the number of layers in the quantum circuit directly impacts computational complexity. To lower computational costs, MicroAlgo employs an Adaptive Circuit Pruning (ACP) method during optimization. This approach dynamically adjusts the circuit structure, eliminating redundant parameters while preserving the classifier's expressive power. As a result, the number of parameters required during training is significantly reduced, leading to a substantial decrease in computational complexity. Hamiltonian Transformation Optimization (HTO): Additionally, MicroAlgo introduces an optimization method based on Hamiltonian transformations. By altering the Hamiltonian representation of the variational quantum circuit, this technique shortens the search path within the parameter space, thereby improving optimization efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that this method can reduce computational complexity by at least an order of magnitude while maintaining classification accuracy. Novel Regularization Strategy to Enhance Training Stability and Generalization Capability: In classical machine learning, regularization methods are widely used to prevent model overfitting. In the realm of quantum machine learning, MicroAlgo introduces a novel quantum regularization strategy called Quantum Entanglement Regularization (QER). This method dynamically adjusts the strength of quantum entanglement during training, preventing the model from overfitting the training data and thereby improving the classifier's generalization ability on unseen data. Additionally, an optimization strategy based on the Energy Landscape is incorporated, which adjusts the shape of the loss function during training. This enables the optimization algorithm to more quickly identify the global optimum, reducing the impact of local optima. Enhanced Noise Robustness for Real Quantum Computing Environments: Given that current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices still exhibit significant noise levels, a model's noise resilience is critical. To improve the classifier's robustness, MicroAlgo proposes a technique based on Variational Quantum Error Correction (VQEC). This method actively learns noise patterns during training and adjusts circuit parameters to mitigate noise effects. This strategy markedly enhances the classifier's stability in noisy environments, making its performance on real quantum devices more reliable. MicroAlgo's classifier auto-optimization technology, based on variational quantum algorithms, successfully reduces the computational complexity of parameter updates through deep optimization of the core circuit and the introduction of novel regularization methods. This approach significantly boosts training speed and generalization capability. This breakthrough technology not only demonstrates its effectiveness in theory but also exhibits superior performance in simulation experiments, laying a crucial foundation for the advancement of quantum machine learning. As quantum computing hardware continues to advance, this technology will further expand its application domains in the future, accelerating the practical implementation of quantum intelligent computing and propelling quantum computing into a new stage of real-world utility. In an era where quantum computing and artificial intelligence converge, this innovation will undoubtedly serve as a significant milestone in advancing the frontiers of technology. About MicroAlgo Inc. MicroAlgo Inc. (the "MicroAlgo"), a Cayman Islands exempted company, is dedicated to the development and application of bespoke central processing algorithms. MicroAlgo provides comprehensive solutions to customers by integrating central processing algorithms with software or hardware, or both, thereby helping them to increase the number of customers, improve end-user satisfaction, achieve direct cost savings, reduce power consumption, and achieve technical goals. The range of MicroAlgo's services includes algorithm optimization, accelerating computing power without the need for hardware upgrades, lightweight data processing, and data intelligence services. MicroAlgo's ability to efficiently deliver software and hardware optimization to customers through bespoke central processing algorithms serves as a driving force for MicroAlgo's long-term development. title: Embedded UI components
summary: We decided to use a shadcn/ui registry to set up our pricing components, instead of a Reactjs library. We used this approach for pricing pages, upgrade and downgrade flows and paywalls.
body_text: We're building Autumn, which is a billing platform that helps devs integrate stripe and manage their pricing model. One feature of this is a UI library to drop-in things like a pricing table, upgrade/downgrade flows, paywalls--similar to Clerk with auth. We are heavy users of shadcn/ui and love having full design customisability. When Supabase launched it’s UI library through shadcn, we wanted to do the same. Here's our exploration into it and some of the challenges we faced. V1 as a React library We first attempted this as a standard npm React library: import PricingPage from "autumn-js" It's biggest issue was customisability**.** There are two ways to make npm components customisable: through props, or a no-code interface in our app. With props there were too many class variables. For example with the pricing page, each pricing card is composed of many headers, descriptions, buttons and more. And each card itself can have variants (recommended, discounts, annual etc). A low code interface is a bad experience for devs, who want full customisability and have 10x experience designing with tailwind/css. Even more so with the era of cursor. This is subjective but I’ve never had a good experience with one. Sidenote: If you ever try to make your npm component customisable via tailwind, all the best. That was one of the most frustrating days of our lives. Also, If you ever forgot what jsx styles look like, here’s a snippet of what we had to write… We made one measly post on linkedin about it, decided it was unusable and shelved it. V2 as shadcn/ui components A few weeks later we started looking into it again with shadcn. npx shadcn@latest add https://ui.useautumn.com/classic/pricing-table.json This immediately felt like a more customizable and fluid DX, but had its own challenges: Because shadcn components install as a user file, we cannot fully control it via our SDK. For example, if we wanted to trigger a modal/popup to confirm a plan upgrade, the user needs to explicitly pass it into a function. This does take away slightly from that “magical DX”. //upgrading to Pro tier < Button onClick ={async () => await attach ({ productId: "pro" , dialog: ProductChangeDialog, }) } />; Since users own and control the component files, deciding what data abstraction level to return to the frontend is hard. For example, our upgrade dialog shows different text and styling depending on the scenarios: - One time purchase vs subscription - Upgrades vs downgrades vs cancellations vs renewals - Does the upgrade require an input from users (eg, quantity of credits to purchase) With a React library, everything would be "completely processed", with no customizability. Initially this is the same approach we took with the shadcn registry, but users quickly told us they wanted to customize the text too. We switched to the "in-between" approach. Our API will return a scenario (eg, upgrade, downgrade, add-on, free-trial etc), and our shadcn components install with a library of cases that users can edit to control the messaging. switch (scenario) { case "scheduled" : return { title: < p >Scheduled product already exists</ p >, message: < p >You will downgrade on { scheduled_date } </ p >, }; case "active" : return { title: < p >Product already active</ p >, message: < p >You are already subscribed to this product.</ p >, }; case "new" : if (recurring) { return { title: < p >Subscribe to { product_name } </ p >, message : ( < p > By clicking confirm, you will be subscribed to { product_name } and your card will be charged immediately. </ p > ), }; } //..... etc Ultimately, after having used it ourselves and watching our users, we’re pretty happy with this approach. Shadcn is as popular as it is for a reason, and we believe in the paradigm of owning your own components and everything inside them. We're maintaining these components for free separate to our main product here: https://pricecn.com

title: Oman: TotalEnergies and OQEP break ground at Marsa LNG
summary: Marsa LNG will be one of the lowest carbon intensity LNG plants in the world Marsa LNG will be the first marine LNG bunkering hub in the Middle East, supporting the shipping industry’s energy transition Paris, May 1, 2025 – Under the patronage of His Excellency Eng. Salim bin Nasser Al Aufi, Minister of Energy […]
body_text: Marsa LNG will be one of the lowest carbon intensity LNG plants in the world Marsa LNG will be the first marine LNG bunkering hub in the Middle East, supporting the shipping industry’s energy transition Paris, May 1, 2025 – Under the patronage of His Excellency Eng. Salim bin Nasser Al Aufi, Minister of Energy & Minerals of the Sultanate of Oman, Patrick Pouyanné, Chairman and CEO of TotalEnergies, and Ahmed Al Azkawi, OQ Exploration and Production CEO, celebrated the ground-breaking of the Marsa LNG plant, in the port of Sohar, northern Oman, one year after the Final Investment Decision . The 1 million ton per year (Mt/y) liquefaction plant is being built by Marsa LNG LLC, a joint company between TotalEnergies (80%) and OQEP (20%). The LNG production, which is expected to start in the first quarter of 2028, is primarily intended to serve the marine fuel market (LNG bunkering) in the Gulf. One of the lowest carbon intensity LNG plants in the world The Marsa LNG plant is fully electrified and combined with a 300 megawatt-peak (MWp) photovoltaic solar farm that will supply the equivalent of the plant’s annual energy needs. Marsa LNG will therefore be one of the lowest carbon intensity LNG plants in the world, with less than 3 kg CO2e/boe of scope 1 and 2 emissions. For reference, this is 90% lower than the average carbon intensity of LNG plants in the world, which stands around 35 kg CO2e/boe1. The first marine LNG bunkering hub in the Middle East Ideally located at the entrance to the Gulf, the Marsa LNG site has been selected to establish the first LNG bunkering hub in the Middle East. A charter contract for a new LNG bunkering vessel has been signed by Marsa LNG LLC. This vessel, named Monte Shams in reference to the Jabal Shams or the “Mountain of the Sun” in north-eastern Oman, is under construction and will be stationed in Sohar from 2028, where it will supply LNG to a wide range of vessels (container ships, tankers, large cruise ships). In the maritime industry, LNG is an immediately available transition fuel allowing a reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by approximately 20% compared to fuel oil. Ships using LNG in Sohar, will further reduce their GHG emissions thanks to the low carbon intensity of the LNG production in Marsa LNG, and local bunkering without the need to transport LNG to a distant bunkering port. "I'm very proud to see Marsa LNG breaking ground, alongside our longstanding partner OQEP, and with the strong support from the Sultanate’s authorities. This flagship project demonstrates that LNG production can be very low carbon, contributing to making gas a long-term transition fuel. With an ambitious technical design, we intend to set the standard and pave the way for the next generation of low-emissions LNG plants across the world. We also offer an effective way to support the shipping sector’s energy transition, by providing lower-emissions marine fuel in a key location at the entrance of the Gulf”, said Patrick Pouyanné, Chairman and CEO of TotalEnergies. Commenting on the groundbreaking of Marsa LNG, His Excellency Salim bin Nasser Al Aufi, Minister of Energy and Minerals , stated : “The Ministry reiterates its steadfast commitment to supporting downstream energy projects as a vital pillar of economic integration across the industrial, trade, port, and logistics sectors. The Marsa LNG project, a strategic collaboration project between OQ Exploration & Production and TotalEnergies, embodies this commitment by developing advanced infrastructure for supplying vessels with LNG as an alternative clean fuel. This project marks a significant step in advancing low-emission energy solutions, reinforcing Oman's position as a reliable regional hub for clean maritime fuel. It aligns with the objectives of Oman Vision 2040, particularly in sustainability and industrial innovation. Additionally, it underscores our dedication to providing responsible energy solutions for the global shipping sector while actively reducing its carbon footprint. While we welcome this pioneering partnership, we affirm that investment in downstream energy projects is a key driver of economic growth, creating quality, sustainable job opportunities, facilitating knowledge transfer, and developing national expertise, all of which strengthen Oman’s readiness to meet the growing demand for sustainable energy sources". "At OQEP, we are committed to driving innovation and sustainability in Oman’s energy landscape. The Marsa LNG project represents a solid step forward, harnessing cutting-edge technology and strategic collaboration to ensure a cleaner, and affordable energy future. As the first LNG bunkering hub in the Middle East, Marsa LNG will play a pivotal role in reducing emissions in the shipping industry while reinforcing Oman’s position as a key player in the global energy sector. We take immense pride in contributing to this transformative journey—one that sets new standards for low-carbon energy solutions", said Ahmed Al Azkawi, CEO of OQEP. 1 Source IEA: The Oil and Gas Industry in Net Zero Transitions report from Nov 2023. ***

title: The Evolution of the Data Analyst role: how AI is reshaping Business Intelligence
summary: AI is transforming data analysis from spreadsheet drudgery to strategic superpower. See how modern analysts are using AI tools to work smarter and deliver…
body_text: Imagine unlocking insights buried within your data in seconds instead of days. You can now have this leap in speed and comprehension with AI-powered data analysis, a workflow that’s making business intelligence faster, smarter, and more intuitive. Gone are the days when data analysts spent countless hours sifting through numbers and spreadsheets to gain actionable insights. Now, with AI integrating into data processes, even non-developers can have decision-making superpowers. AI definitely isn’t replacing data analysts, but it is changing their role. By using AI for tasks like natural language processing, data visualization and automating routine tasks, the next generation of data analysts are completely redefining what it means to work with data. A recent report from Alteryx found that 70% of analysts say AI and automation make them more effective in their roles [2]. There are, to be sure, some challenges that come with this trend. It’s important to balance ethical considerations like data privacy with the massive technological gains from AI. As AI continues to advance, it’s more important than ever for data practitioners to understand its limitations which will ultimately help them use it to its full potential. This article explores some of these themes, helping you understand how to navigate the future of Business Intelligence. The evolution of the data analyst role The role of data analysts has transformed dramatically in recent years. What was once focused on manually retrieving and organizing data has evolved into a position centered on extracting meaningful insights that drive business success. This shift has been accelerated by emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence and advanced analytics tools. Today’s data analysts don’t just compile numbers; they tell compelling stories through data that shape strategic business decisions. The demand for these skilled professionals continues to grow, with projections showing a 23% increase through 2032, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics [1]. This surge reflects the increasing importance of data-driven decision making across industries. Modern data analysts also need to develop soft skills alongside technical abilities. The ability to communicate insights effectively, think critically about data, and understand business context has become just as valuable as technical expertise. By combining these skills, analysts can provide the strategic insights organizations need to thrive in an increasingly competitive landscape. The impact of AI on data analysis AI is fundamentally changing how data analysis works by enabling deeper insights with greater efficiency. With machine learning algorithms and natural language processing technologies, analysts can discover patterns and trends that might otherwise remain hidden. The result? Organizations make faster, better decisions based on comprehensive data insights. The relationship between human analysts and AI is synergistic rather than competitive. Together, they deliver better predictive analytics and generate valuable insights from complex datasets. AI handles the heavy lifting of processing vast amounts of information, while human analysts provide the critical thinking and contextual understanding needed to actually interpret data. By automating routine and time-consuming tasks, AI frees analysts to focus on more strategic aspects of data interpretation. Many experts believe that this shift will elevate the role of data analysis within organizations, transforming it from a primarily technical function to a strategic business driver that directly influences company direction and growth. AI tools helping analysts rather than replacing them AI tools complement human analysts by handling repetitive tasks that previously consumed significant time and resources. These tools excel at data preprocessing, pattern recognition, and basic analysis, allowing human analysts to dedicate their expertise to interpreting results and developing strategic recommendations. Modern AI-powered analytics platforms feature intuitive interfaces that leverage natural language processing. This advancement means analysts can query data using conversational language without needing extensive technical knowledge or coding skills. A product manager can now ask questions like “Show me sales trends for the past quarter” and receive instant visualizations and insights. Rather than eliminating jobs, AI creates opportunities for analysts to engage in more advanced and meaningful work. Tools like Microsoft Power BI demonstrate how user-friendly interfaces can help analysts transform complex data into actionable insights efficiently. This partnership between AI capabilities and human expertise enhances the overall quality and impact of data-driven decisions within organizations. In fact, according to Alteryx’s 2025 State of Data Analysts report, 87% of analysts report that their roles have increased in strategic importance over the past year [3]. Skills required for AI-driven data analysis As organizations increasingly rely on AI and data to drive growth, professionals working in data analysis need a specialized skill set. With these capabilities, they can transform raw data into actionable insights that inform strategic decision-making. While technical knowledge still matters, understanding AI algorithms and committing to continuous learning are equally important for success in this evolving field. Technical skillsets A strong technical foundation forms the backbone of effective AI-driven data analysis. This includes proficiency with data tools and software essential for manipulating and analyzing datasets. Advanced skills in platforms like Power BI let analysts create compelling data narratives through intuitive visualizations that business stakeholders can easily understand. Familiarity with programming languages such as Python or R gives analysts the ability to automate routine tasks and conduct sophisticated analyses. These languages offer powerful libraries specifically designed for data science and machine learning applications, making them invaluable for modern analysts. Understanding database structures and data warehousing concepts supports the efficient management and retrieval of large datasets. This knowledge allows analysts to work with complex data architectures and ensure data quality throughout the analysis process. These technical skills provide the framework within which deeper, AI-driven analytics can flourish. Understanding of AI algorithms For data analysts working with AI tools, having a basic understanding of how AI algorithms function is increasingly valuable. Knowledge of common algorithms like neural networks, decision trees, and clustering methods helps analysts choose the right approach for specific analytical challenges. These algorithms provide the mechanisms through which complex data patterns are identified and understood. For product managers and similar roles, even a foundational understanding of these algorithms improves collaboration with data teams and ensures AI tools deliver desired results aligned with business objectives. As data-driven decisions increasingly rely on algorithmic insights, understanding how these systems work helps in accurately interpreting results and explaining findings to stakeholders. This knowledge empowers analysts to tackle complex problems with solutions that are both technically sound and business-relevant. Continuous learning and upskilling In the rapidly evolving field of AI and data analytics, continuous learning isn’t optional—it’s essential. Technology, algorithms, and methodologies advance at a remarkable pace, making ongoing education necessary to maintain relevance and expertise. For most companies, success will require them to foster a culture of continuous learning so that teams can quickly adopt new tools and apply fresh insights to business challenges. Online courses, industry publications, and professional workshops provide accessible ways for analysts to stay current with emerging trends and technologies. Leaders in data-focused roles, such as chief data officers or analytics managers, play a crucial role in promoting this learning culture. By encouraging skill development and providing learning resources, they improve their organization’s collective capability to leverage data assets effectively and maintain competitive advantage in an increasingly data-driven business environment. The benefits of AI in data analysis The landscape of data analysis is rapidly evolving, with AI transforming how businesses interpret and utilize information. Today’s AI-powered systems help organizations uncover deeper insights and make more informed decisions faster than ever before. These advancements particularly benefit product managers and business leaders who need quick, actionable intelligence to guide product development and business strategy. Chatting with natural language One of the most significant breakthroughs in AI-powered data analysis is the ability to interact with data using natural language. This capability makes data analysis accessible to non-technical team members who previously relied on data specialists for insights. Imagine a product manager typing a question like “How did our new feature impact user engagement last month?” and receiving an immediate, data-backed response. Advanced language models interpret these conversational queries, access relevant data, and respond with clear insights—no SQL knowledge required. This natural language interface removes technical barriers that traditionally limited who could extract value from company data. By democratizing access to data insights, organizations foster a more collaborative and data-informed culture where decisions at all levels benefit from analytical backing. Enhanced data visualization AI significantly improves how data is presented and understood through advanced visualization techniques. These visualizations transform complex datasets into intuitive graphics that communicate trends, patterns, and outliers at a glance. Machine learning algorithms can automatically identify the most meaningful ways to represent specific data types, suggesting optimal visualization formats based on the nature of the information. This intelligence ensures that key insights aren’t lost in overwhelming displays of raw data. For product managers and other decision-makers, these visualizations mean faster comprehension of market trends, user behaviors, and product performance metrics. The ability to grasp complex relationships visually accelerates the decision-making process and helps teams remain agile in the face of market changes. Automation of routine tasks AI excels at automating the repetitive, time-consuming tasks that traditionally occupied much of an analyst’s day. Data cleaning, normalization, and basic processing can now be handled automatically, freeing human analysts for more strategic work. Tasks that once required hours of manual effort can be completed in minutes with greater consistency and fewer errors. Automated data preparation ensures that analysts work with clean, properly structured information, improving the reliability of subsequent analyses. This automation represents a significant efficiency gain for organizations. Teams can process larger datasets faster and move from raw data to actionable insights with less delay. For time-sensitive business decisions, this acceleration can provide a meaningful competitive advantage. Improved decision-making processes The ultimate benefit of AI-powered data analysis is its impact on decision-making quality and speed. By providing deeper insights into market trends, customer behaviors, and operational patterns, AI helps shape more effective strategies. Advanced predictive capabilities allow businesses to anticipate future trends rather than simply react to current conditions. This forward-looking perspective supports proactive planning and helps organizations position themselves advantageously for upcoming market shifts. For product teams specifically, AI-enhanced analytics provide clearer understanding of user needs, pain points, and behaviors. These insights guide product development priorities and feature decisions, ensuring resources are allocated to initiatives with the highest potential value. Navigating ethical considerations in AI-powered analytics As AI becomes increasingly integrated into data analytics workflows, businesses must thoughtfully address the ethical dimensions of these powerful technologies. Proper consideration of these ethical issues isn’t just about compliance—it’s fundamental to maintaining customer trust and building a reputable brand. Data privacy concerns Data privacy stands as a primary concern when implementing AI-powered analytics systems. The collection and processing of large volumes of user data create significant responsibilities for businesses to handle this information ethically and securely. Companies must ensure compliance with data protection regulations like GDPR and CCPA, which mandate transparent data practices and user consent. Implementing robust security measures and maintaining clear data governance frameworks helps protect sensitive information and preserve user trust. Balancing the analytical benefits of comprehensive data collection against privacy considerations requires thoughtful planning. Being transparent with users about data practices and providing clear options for data sharing helps maintain ethical standards while still gathering the insights needed for product improvement. The human element in analysis While AI offers impressive analytical capabilities, the human element is still important. Human analysts bring contextual understanding, ethical judgment, and domain expertise that AI systems can’t replicate. Data analysts play an importantrole in guiding AI systems toward relevant inquiries and interpreting results within the appropriate business context. They ensure that statistics and patterns identified by AI translate into meaningful business actions that align with company values and objectives. This human oversight is particularly important for identifying potential biases in AI models and ensuring that analytical outcomes don’t inadvertently discriminate or reinforce problematic patterns. The most effective approach combines AI’s processing power with human wisdom and ethical awareness. Balancing AI and human insights Finding the right balance between AI capabilities and human insight is a key challenge for organizations adopting AI-powered analytics. The ideal approach leverages the strengths of both to create a system greater than the sum of its parts. AI is great at processing vast datasets, identifying patterns, and performing predictive analysis at scales beyond human capability. Human analysts provide critical context, business acumen, and ethical judgment that shape how these insights are applied. For product teams, this balance might mean using AI to identify usage patterns and market trends while relying on human expertise to interpret these findings within the context of company strategy and customer needs. Creating systems where AI and human intelligence complement each other leads to more nuanced and effective decision-making. Limitations and challenges of AI in data analysis While AI offers tremendous benefits for data analysis, understanding its limitations is essential for effective implementation. Despite impressive capabilities in processing and pattern recognition, AI systems face constraints that businesses should acknowledge when building analytics strategies. Understanding AI’s constraints AI excels at identifying patterns in structured data but often struggles with nuanced interpretation and contextual understanding. Current AI systems lack the intuitive comprehension and creative problem-solving abilities that human analysts bring to complex business questions. For product managers and business leaders, recognizing these limitations helps set appropriate expectations for AI initiatives. While AI can process vast amounts of information quickly, it may miss subtle contextual factors that influence how data should be interpreted for specific business situations. Additionally, AI systems reflect the data they’re trained on, potentially propagating existing biases or limitations in historical datasets. Human oversight remains essential to ensure AI-generated insights align with business realities and ethical standards before being translated into action. Dependency on quality structured data AI systems fundamentally depend on high-quality, well-structured data to produce reliable insights. The adage “garbage in, garbage out” applies particularly strongly to AI-powered analytics. For many organizations, data quality issues present a significant challenge. Inconsistent formatting, missing values, and disorganized data structures can severely limit AI’s effectiveness. Before implementing advanced analytics, companies often need to invest considerable resources in data cleaning and standardization. This dependency on structured data can be especially challenging for businesses with legacy systems or those operating in domains where data collection is inherently messy. Building robust data pipelines and governance practices becomes a prerequisite for successful AI implementation. Misinterpretations and overreliance Perhaps the most subtle challenge with AI-powered analytics is the risk of misinterpretation or overreliance on automated insights. AI systems may identify correlations that are statistically valid but practically meaningless or miss causal relationships that would be obvious to human analysts with domain knowledge. Over-dependence on AI for decision-making can lead organizations to overlook important qualitative factors or unique contextual elements that aren’t captured in their datasets. This risk increases when stakeholders without data science backgrounds interact directly with AI systems without appropriate guidance. The most successful implementations of AI in data analysis maintain healthy skepticism and use AI as one input among many for important decisions. Establishing practices that combine AI-generated insights with human judgment and domain expertise helps mitigate these risks. Using Basedash for AI-powered data analysis In today’s competitive landscape, transforming raw data into actionable insights quickly and efficiently gives businesses a critical advantage. Basedash provides an AI-native business intelligence platform designed specifically to help mid-market companies harness the power of their data without requiring specialized technical expertise. Basedash stands out by combining powerful AI capabilities with an intuitive interface that product managers and business users can navigate easily. The platform automates routine data tasks while providing natural language querying, enhanced visualizations, and predictive analytics capabilities that traditionally required specialized data science teams. For mid-market SaaS companies looking to become more data-driven, Basedash offers a compelling solution that balances sophisticated analytical power with accessibility. By reducing the technical barriers to data insights, Basedash helps organizations make better decisions faster, identify opportunities sooner, and respond to market changes more effectively. Try Basedash today to discover how our AI-native platform can transform your approach to business intelligence and give your team the data insights they need to drive growth and innovation. title: Austin Gold Provides Update on Exploration Activities and Results of the 2025 Annual General Meeting
summary: Austin Gold Corp. was founded in 2020 to focus on gold exploration in Nevada. The Austin Gold team has been instrumental in building several mining successes in the past, including Pretium (“PVG”), SSR Mining (“SSRM”), and Uranerz Energy (acquired by Energy Fuels “UUUU”). Two of those mining companies have multi-billion-dollar market capitalizations.
body_text: May 9, 2025 Summary At Stockade Mountain, the Company has received a permit to drill a water well to produce water for exploration drilling. Planning continues for a reverse circulation (“RC”) drilling program during the summer field season to follow up on encouraging results from the 2023-24 winter drilling program. At Lone Mountain, the Company has begun the 2025 field season that will include geological mapping, geochemical sampling, and additional gravity geophysics. The Company reports the results of its annual general meeting (“AGM”) of shareholders held on May 7, 2025 and changes to officers and directors. Vancouver, BC, Canada — Austin Gold Corp. (“Austin” or the “Company”) (NYSE American: AUST) provides an update on its exploration activities at its Stockade Mountain Project in Oregon, and Lone Mountain and Kelly Creek projects in Nevada, and the results of its AGM of shareholders held on May 7, 2025. Update – Exploration activities At the Stockade Mountain Project , Austin received permission from the Oregon Water Resources Department to drill a water well to produce water for exploration drilling. The Company did not initiate a drill campaign at Stockade late last year as was planned due to mild, wet weather and access road issues. An RC drill program to follow-up on encouraging gold mineralization encountered during the 2023-4 winter drilling program is planned for the summer of 2025. At the Lone Mountain Project , the Company continues to advance exploration with plans for additional geological mapping, geochemical sampling, and gravity geophysics to be conducted during the 2025 field season. In 2024, Austin completed a soil and stream sediment sampling program consisting of 2,027 soil and 122 stream sediment samples. Further analysis of data from the 2024 soil sampling program revealed unusual patterns for a few of the elements that are not normally used for Carlin-type gold deposit exploration. This lessens the confidence of data for the elements that are important. Accordingly, the analytical laboratory will rerun the samples using a different analytical package at no cost to the Company. Although significant historical exploration has been conducted at Lone Mountain, large areas of the property remain untested, or minimally tested, by drilling. At the Kelly Creek Project, Austin continues to determine the best options for further exploration. Robert M. Hatch, the Qualified Person for Austin as defined by National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects , has approved the scientific and technical information in this news release. Results of the 2025 AGM The Company reports the results of its AGM of shareholders held on May 7, 2025 in Vancouver, British Columbia. A total of 7,762,732 shares were represented in person or by proxy at the meeting, being 58.49% of the issued and outstanding shares at the record date. Joe Ovsenek and Ken McNaughton did not stand for re-election. A summary of the AGM results is outlined below. Election of Directors Number Voted For Percentage Voted For Dennis L. Higgs 6,331,179* 99.76% Barbara A. Filas 6,324,621* 99.65% Sandra R. Dennis Higgs has been appointed Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer (previously, President) and Tom Yip has been appointed Lead Independent Director. “On behalf of the Board, I’d like to thank Joe and Ken for their service and contributions to the Company” said Dennis Higgs, Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer. “Looking ahead, we are excited for the prospects of the Company at our mineral projects in this high gold price environment.” About Austin Gold Corp. Austin is a gold exploration company focused on gold targets and making district-scale gold discoveries in the southwestern United States. Austin has two projects in Nevada. The Kelly Creek Project is located on the Battle Mountain—Eureka (Cortez) gold trend in Humboldt County and the Lone Mountain Project is on the Independence-Jerritt Canyon gold trend in Elko County. Collectively, these Nevada properties comprise approximately 34.9 mi2 (90 km2) of unpatented lode mining claims and private property.
